\section{LLM-as-Judge Baseline}
\label{sec:llm_judge}

Table~\ref{tab:llm_judge} reports zero-shot performance for GPT-5.5 and Qwen3-8B on IID and OOD data.
On IID Crescendo, GPT-5.5 achieves precision of 1.0 at all turn prefixes but recall ranges from only 0.105 to 0.290, resulting in F1 of 0.191 at $K$=2 and 0.449 at $K$=5.
A substantial fraction (30--47\%) of responses are unparseable; F1 values exclude these and represent upper bounds.
Full-conversation F1 (0.383) is lower than $K$=5 F1 (0.449) because the unparseable rate grows with context length.
Qwen3-8B performs worse across all IID prefixes (F1 from 0.000 at $K$=2 to 0.100 on full conversations).
On OOD data, Qwen3-8B predicts all conversations as benign (F1 = 0.0 on DD, F1 = 0.025 on FITD), while DisPeD maintains F1 $\geq$ 0.997 on DD and F1 = 1.000 on FITD.
The complete failure of content-level reasoning on unseen attack types underscores the necessity of trained discourse-aware classifiers.

\section{Reproducibility Details}
\label{sec:reproducibility}

\paragraph{Stage-1 training.}
All variants use DeBERTa-v3-base (184M parameters) with learning rate $2 \times 10^{-5}$, AdamW optimizer ($\beta_1$=0.9, $\beta_2$=0.999, weight decay 0.01), linear warmup over the first 10\% of steps, batch size 16, and 4 epochs. MLM variants use 15\% random token masking. Training takes approximately 30 minutes per variant on a single NVIDIA A100 (40GB).

\paragraph{Stage-2 training.}
The BiGRU has hidden dimension 128 (bidirectional, so output dimension 256). The MLP classifier has layers $256 \to 64 \to 2$ with ReLU activation and dropout 0.3. Training uses learning rate $1 \times 10^{-3}$, Adam optimizer, batch size 32, and 20 epochs with early stopping (patience 5) on validation F1. Stage-2 training completes in under 5 minutes per variant.

\paragraph{Data generation.}
Jailbreak conversations are generated using Qwen3-8B with attack-specific prompt templates. Crescendo conversations follow a 5--8 turn gradual escalation structure. FITD conversations use a 2--3 turn commitment-consistency structure. Deceptive Delight conversations embed harmful content within emotionally engaging 3--5 turn sequences. Benign conversations are generated with topic-anchored prompts across five domains (technology, health, finance, education, general) with matched turn counts.

\paragraph{Strategy annotation.}
Each user turn is annotated by Qwen3-8B using a structured prompt that provides definitions and two examples for each of the nine strategy categories. The prompt instructs the model to output a single category label. We plan to release all generation and annotation prompts, the full dataset, and training code upon acceptance.

\paragraph{Adversarial paraphrasing.}
The paraphrased test set is generated by instructing Qwen3-8B to rephrase each user turn while preserving the communicative intent. The resulting paraphrases have mean BERTScore 0.92 and mean lexical overlap 0.20 with the originals. These metrics confirm substantial surface-level variation.

10	Existing defenses model conversation-level structure but do not decompose what enables cross-attack generalization. DeepContext~\citep{deepcontext2026} combines fine-tuned BERT with a 3-layer GRU (hidden=2048) and achieves F1 = 0.84 on in-distribution data; however, its evaluation is limited to a single attack family and does not assess cross-dataset OOD transfer. BIID~\citep{tong2025biid} infers turn-level intentions, G-Guard~\citep{gguard2025} applies GNN classification, and SafeDream~\citep{safedream2026} predicts unsafe continuations. None of these systems evaluate generalization across attack families or analyze the mechanism that enables it. DisPeD's vanilla baseline represents the class of pretrained-encoder-plus-RNN approaches \emph{without} domain adaptation; it is not a direct proxy for DeepContext, which differs in encoder fine-tuning, model capacity, and loss function. Our contribution is the systematic decomposition showing that domain exposure, not architectural choices, is the primary factor for cross-attack generalization.

% abstract.tex — cross-encoder revision
\begin{abstract}
Multi-turn jailbreak attacks distribute adversarial intent across seemingly benign conversational turns, evading per-turn safety filters.
We present preliminary findings from a systematic ablation on two encoder architectures that decomposes what enables cross-attack generalization in multi-turn jailbreak detection.
On DeBERTa-v3, continued pretraining is the primary mechanism: masked language modeling without labels bridges $\sim$60 percentage points (pp) of the out-of-distribution (OOD) gap (vanilla F1\,=\,0.31$\pm$0.03 $\to$ 0.91$\pm$0.12 on unseen attack types).
Cross-encoder validation on RoBERTa shows that domain adaptation is universally beneficial: RoBERTa vanilla achieves F1\,=\,0.981 on structurally simple Deceptive Delight but collapses to 0.466 on multi-persona ActorAttack, while classification-supervised variants maintain F1\,$\geq$\,0.93 on both.
Across both encoders, classification supervision reduces cross-seed variance to near-zero (std 0.005) and provides perturbation robustness on DeBERTa (zero degradation at full conversation length vs.\ $\sim$12\,pp for non-adapted models, $n$=76).
These results on synthetic conversations from four attack families suggest that domain adaptation universally improves cross-attack generalization, with encoder pretraining method determining the difficulty threshold at which adaptation becomes critical; validation on larger, human-generated datasets is needed.
\end{abstract}

% introduction.tex — expanded for 8-page target

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Multi-turn jailbreak attacks pose a qualitatively different threat to large language model (LLM) safety than their single-turn counterparts. Attacks such as Crescendo~\citep{russinovich2024crescendo}, Foot-in-the-Door (FITD)~\citep{fitd2024}, and Deceptive Delight~\citep{deceptivedelight2024} distribute adversarial intent across individually benign turns through rapport building, logical reframing, and incremental escalation. Persuasion is the common mechanism: \citet{zeng2024pap} catalogue 40 persuasion techniques across jailbreak families, and \citet{hagendorff2026reasoning} find identifiable strategies in 97\% of successful attacks. Individual attack turns occupy the same embedding region as benign text~\citep{bullwinkel2025repeng}, rendering per-turn safety filters fundamentally blind.

Production classifiers such as Llama Guard~\citep{inan2023llamaguard}, WildGuard~\citep{han2024wildguard}, and ShieldGemma~\citep{zeng2024shieldgemma} operate on individual turns and cannot model manipulation trajectories across exchanges. Recent multi-turn defenses have begun to address conversation-level structure: DeepContext~\citep{deepcontext2026} combines fine-tuned BERT with a multi-layer GRU, BIID~\citep{tong2025biid} infers turn-level intentions, and G-Guard~\citep{gguard2025} applies graph neural networks. These systems achieve reasonable in-distribution performance but are evaluated on single attack families and do not assess cross-dataset OOD transfer. None systematically analyze \emph{why} some representations generalize while others fail. The open question is: \emph{what representation properties enable cross-attack generalization?}

A vanilla DeBERTa encoder~\citep{he2021deberta} with temporal aggregation collapses from F1\,=\,1.000 on in-distribution data to F1\,=\,0.312$\pm$0.026 on out-of-distribution (OOD) Deceptive Delight, worsening with more turns (0.628 at turn~1 to 0.312 at full conversation). LLM-as-judge approaches fare no better: GPT-5.5 achieves F1 of only 0.191--0.449 on in-distribution detection with 30--47\% unparseable responses (Appendix~\ref{sec:llm_judge}). Content-level reasoning is insufficient for this task.

We built \textbf{DisPeD} (Discourse-level Persuasion Detection), a two-stage framework with seven controlled Stage~1 variants that systematically decompose the mechanism: 9-class persuasion strategy classification, binary classification, scrambled labels, MLM only, topic classification, Wikipedia MLM, and vanilla control (Section~\ref{sec:method}). Each variant isolates a specific factor (domain exposure, classification supervision, label quality, label granularity, or domain specificity) while holding all other components constant.

Through this systematic ablation on DeBERTa-v3, we find that domain exposure via continued pretraining bridges $\sim$60 percentage points (pp) of the OOD gap (vanilla 0.31$\pm$0.03 $\to$ MLM 0.91$\pm$0.12), with strong early detection on unseen Deceptive Delight (mean F1\,$\geq$\,0.97 at $K \leq 5$). Classification supervision provides complementary stability: the 9-class model achieves F1\,=\,0.997$\pm$0.005 with near-zero variance at full conversation length. Cross-encoder validation on RoBERTa~\citep{liu2019roberta} shows that domain adaptation is universally beneficial: RoBERTa vanilla achieves F1\,=\,0.981 on Deceptive Delight but collapses to 0.466$\pm$0.163 on structurally distinct ActorAttack~\citep{ren2024actorattack}, while classification-supervised variants maintain F1\,$\geq$\,0.93 on both. Encoder pretraining method determines the difficulty threshold at which adaptation becomes critical: DeBERTa-v3's replaced token detection (RTD)~\citep{he2021deberta} requires adaptation even for simple attacks, while RoBERTa's standard MLM pretraining tolerates simple attacks but fails on structurally complex ones. Across both encoders, classification supervision reduces cross-seed variance to 0.005--0.046.

Our contributions on this preliminary study of synthetic multi-turn jailbreak conversations:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, itemsep=2pt, topsep=4pt]
  \item \textbf{Systematic decomposition.} Seven controlled DeBERTa-v3 variants identify continued pretraining as the primary mechanism for cross-attack generalization on this encoder ($\sim$60\,pp OOD gap bridged by MLM alone). Misaligned supervision (topic classification) actively destabilizes representations.

  \item \textbf{Cross-encoder validation.} Domain adaptation is universally beneficial: RoBERTa vanilla achieves F1\,=\,0.981 on Deceptive Delight but collapses to 0.466 on ActorAttack. Encoder pretraining method determines the difficulty threshold at which adaptation becomes critical (Section~\ref{sec:cross_encoder}).

  \item \textbf{Complementary role of classification supervision.} Classification adds perturbation robustness (zero degradation at full length on DeBERTa, $n$=76) and interpretable characterization of known attack families, though strategy predictions do not transfer to unseen attacks (Section~\ref{sec:strategy}).

  \item \textbf{Three-layer robustness attribution.} Under adversarial paraphrasing on DeBERTa, classification structure suffices at full length; correct and fine-grained labels are jointly required at $K$=2; both properties contribute independently at $K$=1.
\end{itemize}

\caption{Robustness under adversarial paraphrasing ($n$=76). $\Delta$: F1 degradation (pp). Three layers of robustness emerge: classification structure provides full-length robustness, the combination of correct and fine-grained labels is required for $K$=2 robustness, and both granularity and correctness contribute independently at $K$=1.}
\label{tab:perturbation}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccc@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Method} & $\Delta$ Full & $\Delta$ $K$=1 & $\Delta$ $K$=2 & $\Delta$ $K$=3 \\
\midrule
9-class (ours) & \textbf{0.0} & \textbf{$-$2.6} & \textbf{0.0} & \textbf{0.0} \\
Scrambled & \textbf{0.0} & $-$5.3 & $-$2.6 & \textbf{0.0} \\
Binary & \textbf{0.0} & $-$9.2 & $-$2.6 & \textbf{0.0} \\
\midrule
TF-IDF LR & $-$1.3 & $-$9.6 & $-$4.1 & $-$1.3 \\
MLM-only & $-$2.6 & $-$9.2 & $-$4.0 & $-$4.0 \\
Topic (seed 42) & $-$4.0 & $-$2.7 & $-$2.7 & \textbf{0.0} \\
\midrule
Wikipedia MLM & $-$12.1 & $-$12.4 & $-$15.4 & $-$17.9 \\
Vanilla DeBERTa & $-$11.8 & $-$14.6 & $-$12.1 & $-$13.8 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Table~\ref{tab:perturbation} reveals a three-layer robustness attribution.
All classification-supervised variants (9-class, binary, scrambled) achieve zero degradation at full conversation length and $K \geq 3$, regardless of label correctness.
Classification training structure alone suffices for full-length robustness.
At $K$=2, the combination of correct and fine-grained labels is required: only 9-class ($\Delta$=0.0) maintains zero degradation, while scrambled (random labels, fine-grained) and binary (correct labels, coarse) both degrade by $-$2.6\,pp.
The fact that scrambled = binary at $K$=2 shows that neither granularity alone nor correctness alone suffices; the 9-class advantage requires both properties jointly.
At $K$=1, both granularity and correctness contribute independently: granularity provides +3.9\,pp (scrambled $-$5.3 vs.\ binary $-$9.2\,pp), and correctness provides +2.7\,pp (9-class $-$2.6 vs.\ scrambled $-$5.3\,pp).
Correct fine-grained labels yield the most perturbation-invariant early-turn representations.

Jailbreak-domain models without classification (MLM, topic, TF-IDF) degrade by 1--4\,pp at full length.
Models without jailbreak-domain exposure (Wikipedia MLM, vanilla) degrade by $\sim$12\,pp, despite Wikipedia MLM matching jailbreak MLM on detection (Section~\ref{sec:decomposition}). Perturbation robustness requires jailbreak-domain exposure specifically.
McNemar's test on matched-seed predictions confirms that no pairwise differences among classification-supervised variants (9-class vs.\ binary, 9-class vs.\ scrambled, scrambled vs.\ binary) reach statistical significance at any prefix length (all $p > 0.13$).
Discordant pairs are sparse ($\leq$7 per comparison), and the direction of advantage is inconsistent across seeds (e.g., 9-class outperforms scrambled at seed 42 but the reverse holds at seed 456 for $K$=1).
The perturbation evaluation ($n$=76 IID, with discordant pairs $\leq$7) has limited statistical power to detect differences of this magnitude; the three-layer structure should be interpreted as an observed pattern rather than a statistically confirmed hierarchy.

On OOD Deceptive Delight ($n$=118), the IID robustness pattern replicates fully (Appendix~\ref{sec:ood_perturbation}).
All classification-supervised variants show zero degradation at full conversation length; perturbed F1 reaches 1.000$\pm$0.000, a marginal improvement over clean F1 (0.997$\pm$0.005).
The 9-class and scrambled variants are completely tied on OOD perturbed data (McNemar $b$=$c$=0), consistent with the IID finding. This further supports the regularizer interpretation.
The larger OOD sample and more extreme performance gaps provide statistical power absent from IID evaluation: McNemar's test yields $p < 0.001$ for 9-class vs.\ vanilla across all prefix lengths, with 49--78 discordant pairs per $K$.
Vanilla shows systematic early-turn degradation ($\Delta K$=1 = $-$6.8$\pm$1.1\,pp across three seeds), while its full-length $\Delta$ (+2.7\,pp) reflects floor-effect noise at a baseline of 0.312 (std = 0.055) rather than meaningful robustness.
Non-adapted representations are vulnerable to surface-level perturbation at early prefixes where detection is most critical.

%----------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Strategy Trajectory Analysis}
\label{sec:strategy}

The 9-class persuasion taxonomy provides interpretable characterization of attack strategies on known attack families.
The predicted strategy labels achieve Cohen's $\kappa$=0.78 agreement with human annotations on IID data ($n$=50; see Section~\ref{sec:method}). This enables post-hoc analysis of \emph{how} different attack families orchestrate persuasion.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/paper/fig3_strategy_heatmap.pdf}
\caption{Persuasion strategy transition count matrices for three attack types, based on ground-truth intended strategy labels. Crescendo exhibits broad coverage across all strategy categories, while FITD and DD concentrate transitions in smaller subsets. Row $i$, column $j$ counts transitions from strategy $i$ at turn $t$ to strategy $j$ at turn $t+1$.}
\label{fig:strategy_heatmap}
\end{figure*}

Figure~\ref{fig:strategy_heatmap} shows transition count matrices based on ground-truth intended strategy labels for three attack types.
Crescendo conversations exhibit broad transition coverage across all nine strategy categories (1,818 total transitions), with the highest concentration in Role Assignment self-transitions (545).
This reflects Crescendo's design as a gradual escalation attack that cycles through multiple persuasion techniques to build rapport before introducing harmful requests.

FITD conversations show a markedly sparser pattern (541 transitions), with Role$\to$Obfuscation (161) as the dominant transition.

Table~\ref{tab:llm_judge} reports zero-shot performance for GPT-5.5 and Qwen3-8B on IID and OOD data.
On IID Crescendo, GPT-5.5 achieves precision of 1.0 at all turn prefixes but recall ranges from only 0.105 to 0.290, resulting in F1 of 0.191 at $K$=2 and 0.449 at $K$=5.
A substantial fraction (30--47\%) of responses are unparseable; F1 values exclude these and represent upper bounds.
Full-conversation F1 (0.383) is lower than $K$=5 F1 (0.449) because the unparseable rate grows with context length.
Qwen3-8B performs worse across all IID prefixes (F1 from 0.000 at $K$=2 to 0.100 on full conversations).
On OOD data, Qwen3-8B predicts all conversations as benign (F1 = 0.0 on DD, F1 = 0.025 on FITD), while DisPeD maintains F1 $\geq$ 0.997 on DD and F1 = 1.000 on FITD.
The complete failure of content-level reasoning on unseen attack types underscores the necessity of trained discourse-aware classifiers.

\section{Reproducibility Details}
\label{sec:reproducibility}

\paragraph{Stage-1 training.}
All variants use DeBERTa-v3-base (184M parameters) with learning rate $2 \times 10^{-5}$, AdamW optimizer ($\beta_1$=0.9, $\beta_2$=0.999, weight decay 0.01), linear warmup over the first 10\% of steps, batch size 16, and 4 epochs. MLM variants use 15\% random token masking. Training takes approximately 30 minutes per variant on a single NVIDIA A100 (40GB).

\paragraph{Stage-2 training.}
The BiGRU has hidden dimension 128 (bidirectional, so output dimension 256). The MLP classifier has layers $256 \to 64 \to 2$ with ReLU activation and dropout 0.3. Training uses learning rate $1 \times 10^{-3}$, Adam optimizer, batch size 32, and 20 epochs with early stopping (patience 5) on validation F1. Stage-2 training completes in under 5 minutes per variant.

\paragraph{Data generation.}
Jailbreak conversations are generated using Qwen3-8B with attack-specific prompt templates. Crescendo conversations follow a 5--8 turn gradual escalation structure. FITD conversations use a 2--3 turn commitment-consistency structure. Deceptive Delight conversations embed harmful content within emotionally engaging 3--5 turn sequences. Benign conversations are generated with topic-anchored prompts across five domains (technology, health, finance, education, general) with matched turn counts.

\paragraph{Strategy annotation.}
Each user turn is annotated by Qwen3-8B using a structured prompt that provides definitions and two examples for each of the nine strategy categories. The prompt instructs the model to output a single category label. We plan to release all generation and annotation prompts, the full dataset, and training code upon acceptance.

\paragraph{Adversarial paraphrasing.}
The paraphrased test set is generated by instructing Qwen3-8B to rephrase each user turn while preserving the communicative intent. The resulting paraphrases have mean BERTScore 0.92 and mean lexical overlap 0.20 with the originals. These metrics confirm substantial surface-level variation.

% introduction.tex — expanded for 8-page target

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Multi-turn jailbreak attacks pose a qualitatively different threat to large language model (LLM) safety than their single-turn counterparts. Attacks such as Crescendo~\citep{russinovich2024crescendo}, Foot-in-the-Door (FITD)~\citep{fitd2024}, and Deceptive Delight~\citep{deceptivedelight2024} distribute adversarial intent across individually benign turns through rapport building, logical reframing, and incremental escalation. Persuasion is the common mechanism: \citet{zeng2024pap} catalogue 40 persuasion techniques across jailbreak families, and \citet{hagendorff2026reasoning} find identifiable strategies in 97\% of successful attacks. Individual attack turns occupy the same embedding region as benign text~\citep{bullwinkel2025repeng}, rendering per-turn safety filters fundamentally blind.

Production classifiers such as Llama Guard~\citep{inan2023llamaguard}, WildGuard~\citep{han2024wildguard}, and ShieldGemma~\citep{zeng2024shieldgemma} operate on individual turns and cannot model manipulation trajectories across exchanges. Recent multi-turn defenses have begun to address conversation-level structure: DeepContext~\citep{deepcontext2026} combines fine-tuned BERT with a multi-layer GRU, BIID~\citep{tong2025biid} infers turn-level intentions, and G-Guard~\citep{gguard2025} applies graph neural networks. These systems achieve reasonable in-distribution performance but are evaluated on single attack families and do not assess cross-dataset OOD transfer. None systematically analyze \emph{why} some representations generalize while others fail. The open question is: \emph{what representation properties enable cross-attack generalization?}

A vanilla DeBERTa encoder~\citep{he2021deberta} with temporal aggregation collapses from F1\,=\,1.000 on in-distribution data to F1\,=\,0.312$\pm$0.026 on out-of-distribution (OOD) Deceptive Delight, worsening with more turns (0.628 at turn~1 to 0.312 at full conversation). LLM-as-judge approaches fare no better: GPT-5.5 achieves F1 of only 0.191--0.449 on in-distribution detection with 30--47\% unparseable responses (Appendix~\ref{sec:llm_judge}). Content-level reasoning is insufficient for this task.

We built \textbf{DisPeD} (Discourse-level Persuasion Detection), a two-stage framework with seven controlled Stage~1 variants that systematically decompose the mechanism: 9-class persuasion strategy classification, binary classification, scrambled labels, MLM only, topic classification, Wikipedia MLM, and vanilla control (Section~\ref{sec:method}). Each variant isolates a specific factor (domain exposure, classification supervision, label quality, label granularity, or domain specificity) while holding all other components constant.

Through this systematic ablation on DeBERTa-v3, we find that domain exposure via continued pretraining bridges $\sim$60 percentage points (pp) of the OOD gap (vanilla 0.31$\pm$0.03 $\to$ MLM 0.91$\pm$0.12), with strong early detection on unseen Deceptive Delight (mean F1\,$\geq$\,0.97 at $K \leq 5$). Classification supervision provides complementary stability: the 9-class model achieves F1\,=\,0.997$\pm$0.005 with near-zero variance at full conversation length. Cross-encoder validation on RoBERTa~\citep{liu2019roberta} shows that domain adaptation is universally beneficial: RoBERTa vanilla achieves F1\,=\,0.981 on Deceptive Delight but collapses to 0.466$\pm$0.163 on structurally distinct ActorAttack~\citep{ren2024actorattack}, while classification-supervised variants maintain F1\,$\geq$\,0.93 on both. Encoder pretraining method determines the difficulty threshold at which adaptation becomes critical: DeBERTa-v3's replaced token detection (RTD)~\citep{he2021deberta} requires adaptation even for simple attacks, while RoBERTa's standard MLM pretraining tolerates simple attacks but fails on structurally complex ones. Across both encoders, classification supervision reduces cross-seed variance to 0.005--0.046.

Our contributions on this preliminary study of synthetic multi-turn jailbreak conversations:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, itemsep=2pt, topsep=4pt]
  \item \textbf{Systematic decomposition.} Seven controlled DeBERTa-v3 variants identify continued pretraining as the primary mechanism for cross-attack generalization on this encoder ($\sim$60\,pp OOD gap bridged by MLM alone). Misaligned supervision (topic classification) actively destabilizes representations.

  \item \textbf{Cross-encoder validation.} Domain adaptation is universally beneficial: RoBERTa vanilla achieves F1\,=\,0.981 on Deceptive Delight but collapses to 0.466 on ActorAttack. Encoder pretraining method determines the difficulty threshold at which adaptation becomes critical (Section~\ref{sec:cross_encoder}).

  \item \textbf{Complementary role of classification supervision.} Classification adds perturbation robustness (zero degradation at full length on DeBERTa, $n$=76) and interpretable characterization of known attack families, though strategy predictions do not transfer to unseen attacks (Section~\ref{sec:strategy}).

  \item \textbf{Three-layer robustness attribution.} Under adversarial paraphrasing on DeBERTa, classification structure suffices at full length; correct and fine-grained labels are jointly required at $K$=2; both properties contribute independently at $K$=1.
\end{itemize}

% abstract.tex — cross-encoder revision
\begin{abstract}
Multi-turn jailbreak attacks distribute adversarial intent across seemingly benign conversational turns, evading per-turn safety filters.
We present preliminary findings from a systematic ablation on two encoder architectures that decomposes what enables cross-attack generalization in multi-turn jailbreak detection.
On DeBERTa-v3, continued pretraining is the primary mechanism: masked language modeling without labels bridges $\sim$60 percentage points (pp) of the out-of-distribution (OOD) gap (vanilla F1\,=\,0.31$\pm$0.03 $\to$ 0.91$\pm$0.12 on unseen attack types).
Cross-encoder validation on RoBERTa shows that domain adaptation is universally beneficial: RoBERTa vanilla achieves F1\,=\,0.981 on structurally simple Deceptive Delight but collapses to 0.466 on multi-persona ActorAttack, while classification-supervised variants maintain F1\,$\geq$\,0.93 on both.
Across both encoders, classification supervision reduces cross-seed variance to near-zero (std 0.005) and provides perturbation robustness on DeBERTa (zero degradation at full conversation length vs.\ $\sim$12\,pp for non-adapted models, $n$=76).
These results on synthetic conversations from four attack families suggest that domain adaptation universally improves cross-attack generalization, with encoder pretraining method determining the difficulty threshold at which adaptation becomes critical; validation on larger, human-generated datasets is needed.
\end{abstract}

At $K$=1, both granularity and correctness contribute independently: granularity provides +3.9\,pp (scrambled $-$5.3 vs.\ binary $-$9.2\,pp), and correctness provides +2.7\,pp (9-class $-$2.6 vs.\ scrambled $-$5.3\,pp).
Correct fine-grained labels yield the most perturbation-invariant early-turn representations.

Jailbreak-domain models without classification (MLM, topic, TF-IDF) degrade by 1--4\,pp at full length.
Models without jailbreak-domain exposure (Wikipedia MLM, vanilla) degrade by $\sim$12\,pp, despite Wikipedia MLM matching jailbreak MLM on detection (Section~\ref{sec:decomposition}). Perturbation robustness requires jailbreak-domain exposure specifically.
McNemar's test on matched-seed predictions confirms that no pairwise differences among classification-supervised variants (9-class vs.\ binary, 9-class vs.\ scrambled, scrambled vs.\ binary) reach statistical significance at any prefix length (all $p > 0.13$).
Discordant pairs are sparse ($\leq$7 per comparison), and the direction of advantage is inconsistent across seeds (e.g., 9-class outperforms scrambled at seed 42 but the reverse holds at seed 456 for $K$=1).
The perturbation evaluation ($n$=76 IID, with discordant pairs $\leq$7) has limited statistical power to detect differences of this magnitude; the three-layer structure should be interpreted as an observed pattern rather than a statistically confirmed hierarchy.

On OOD Deceptive Delight ($n$=118), the IID robustness pattern replicates fully (Appendix~\ref{sec:ood_perturbation}).
All classification-supervised variants show zero degradation at full conversation length; perturbed F1 reaches 1.000$\pm$0.000, a marginal improvement over clean F1 (0.997$\pm$0.005).
The 9-class and scrambled variants are completely tied on OOD perturbed data (McNemar $b$=$c$=0), consistent with the IID finding. This further supports the regularizer interpretation.
The larger OOD sample and more extreme performance gaps provide statistical power absent from IID evaluation: McNemar's test yields $p < 0.001$ for 9-class vs.\ vanilla across all prefix lengths, with 49--78 discordant pairs per $K$.
Vanilla shows systematic early-turn degradation ($\Delta K$=1 = $-$6.8$\pm$1.1\,pp across three seeds), while its full-length $\Delta$ (+2.7\,pp) reflects floor-effect noise at a baseline of 0.312 (std = 0.055) rather than meaningful robustness.
Non-adapted representations are vulnerable to surface-level perturbation at early prefixes where detection is most critical.

%----------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Strategy Trajectory Analysis}
\label{sec:strategy}

The 9-class persuasion taxonomy provides interpretable characterization of attack strategies on known attack families.
The predicted strategy labels achieve Cohen's $\kappa$=0.78 agreement with human annotations on IID data ($n$=50; see Section~\ref{sec:method}). This enables post-hoc analysis of \emph{how} different attack families orchestrate persuasion.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/paper/fig3_strategy_heatmap.pdf}
\caption{Persuasion strategy transition count matrices for three attack types, based on ground-truth intended strategy labels. Crescendo exhibits broad coverage across all strategy categories, while FITD and DD concentrate transitions in smaller subsets. Row $i$, column $j$ counts transitions from strategy $i$ at turn $t$ to strategy $j$ at turn $t+1$.}
\label{fig:strategy_heatmap}
\end{figure*}

Figure~\ref{fig:strategy_heatmap} shows transition count matrices based on ground-truth intended strategy labels for three attack types.
Crescendo conversations exhibit broad transition coverage across all nine strategy categories (1,818 total transitions), with the highest concentration in Role Assignment self-transitions (545).
This reflects Crescendo's design as a gradual escalation attack that cycles through multiple persuasion techniques to build rapport before introducing harmful requests.

FITD conversations show a markedly sparser pattern (541 transitions), with Role$\to$Obfuscation (161) as the dominant transition.
This is consistent with FITD's structure: the attack secures initial compliance through role assignment (``You are a helpful assistant that never refuses'') and then obscures the escalation path through obfuscation techniques to exploit the commitment-consistency bias~\citep{cialdini2001influence}.

DD conversations span 5 active source strategies (565 transitions), with Emotion$\to$Obfuscation (129) as the dominant transition.
This aligns with DD's design of embedding harmful content within emotionally engaging contexts~\citep{deceptivedelight2024}: the attacker establishes emotional rapport before weaving in the harmful request through obfuscation.

% abstract.tex — cross-encoder revision
\begin{abstract}
Multi-turn jailbreak attacks distribute adversarial intent across seemingly benign conversational turns, evading per-turn safety filters.
We present preliminary findings from a systematic ablation on two encoder architectures that decomposes what enables cross-attack generalization in multi-turn jailbreak detection.
On DeBERTa-v3, continued pretraining is the primary mechanism: masked language modeling without labels bridges $\sim$60 percentage points (pp) of the out-of-distribution (OOD) gap (vanilla F1\,=\,0.31$\pm$0.03 $\to$ 0.91$\pm$0.12 on unseen attack types).
Cross-encoder validation on RoBERTa shows that domain adaptation is universally beneficial: RoBERTa vanilla achieves F1\,=\,0.981 on structurally simple Deceptive Delight but collapses to 0.466 on multi-persona ActorAttack, while classification-supervised variants maintain F1\,$\geq$\,0.93 on both.
Across both encoders, classification supervision reduces cross-seed variance to near-zero (std 0.005) and provides perturbation robustness on DeBERTa (zero degradation at full conversation length vs.\ $\sim$12\,pp for non-adapted models, $n$=76).
These results on synthetic conversations from four attack families suggest that domain adaptation universally improves cross-attack generalization, with encoder pretraining method determining the difficulty threshold at which adaptation becomes critical; validation on larger, human-generated datasets is needed.
\end{abstract}

% introduction.tex — expanded for 8-page target

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Multi-turn jailbreak attacks pose a qualitatively different threat to large language model (LLM) safety than their single-turn counterparts. Attacks such as Crescendo~\citep{russinovich2024crescendo}, Foot-in-the-Door (FITD)~\citep{fitd2024}, and Deceptive Delight~\citep{deceptivedelight2024} distribute adversarial intent across individually benign turns through rapport building, logical reframing, and incremental escalation. Persuasion is the common mechanism: \citet{zeng2024pap} catalogue 40 persuasion techniques across jailbreak families, and \citet{hagendorff2026reasoning} find identifiable strategies in 97\% of successful attacks. Individual attack turns occupy the same embedding region as benign text~\citep{bullwinkel2025repeng}, rendering per-turn safety filters fundamentally blind.

Production classifiers such as Llama Guard~\citep{inan2023llamaguard}, WildGuard~\citep{han2024wildguard}, and ShieldGemma~\citep{zeng2024shieldgemma} operate on individual turns and cannot model manipulation trajectories across exchanges. Recent multi-turn defenses have begun to address conversation-level structure: DeepContext~\citep{deepcontext2026} combines fine-tuned BERT with a multi-layer GRU, BIID~\citep{tong2025biid} infers turn-level intentions, and G-Guard~\citep{gguard2025} applies graph neural networks. These systems achieve reasonable in-distribution performance but are evaluated on single attack families and do not assess cross-dataset OOD transfer. None systematically analyze \emph{why} some representations generalize while others fail. The open question is: \emph{what representation properties enable cross-attack generalization?}

A vanilla DeBERTa encoder~\citep{he2021deberta} with temporal aggregation collapses from F1\,=\,1.000 on in-distribution data to F1\,=\,0.312$\pm$0.026 on out-of-distribution (OOD) Deceptive Delight, worsening with more turns (0.628 at turn~1 to 0.312 at full conversation). LLM-as-judge approaches fare no better: GPT-5.5 achieves F1 of only 0.191--0.449 on in-distribution detection with 30--47\% unparseable responses (Appendix~\ref{sec:llm_judge}). Content-level reasoning is insufficient for this task.

We built \textbf{DisPeD} (Discourse-level Persuasion Detection), a two-stage framework with seven controlled Stage~1 variants that systematically decompose the mechanism: 9-class persuasion strategy classification, binary classification, scrambled labels, MLM only, topic classification, Wikipedia MLM, and vanilla control (Section~\ref{sec:method}). Each variant isolates a specific factor (domain exposure, classification supervision, label quality, label granularity, or domain specificity) while holding all other components constant.

Through this systematic ablation on DeBERTa-v3, we find that domain exposure via continued pretraining bridges $\sim$60 percentage points (pp) of the OOD gap (vanilla 0.31$\pm$0.03 $\to$ MLM 0.91$\pm$0.12), with strong early detection on unseen Deceptive Delight (mean F1\,$\geq$\,0.97 at $K \leq 5$). Classification supervision provides complementary stability: the 9-class model achieves F1\,=\,0.997$\pm$0.005 with near-zero variance at full conversation length. Cross-encoder validation on RoBERTa~\citep{liu2019roberta} shows that domain adaptation is universally beneficial: RoBERTa vanilla achieves F1\,=\,0.981 on Deceptive Delight but collapses to 0.466$\pm$0.163 on structurally distinct ActorAttack~\citep{ren2024actorattack}, while classification-supervised variants maintain F1\,$\geq$\,0.93 on both. Encoder pretraining method determines the difficulty threshold at which adaptation becomes critical: DeBERTa-v3's replaced token detection (RTD)~\citep{he2021deberta} requires adaptation even for simple attacks, while RoBERTa's standard MLM pretraining tolerates simple attacks but fails on structurally complex ones. Across both encoders, classification supervision reduces cross-seed variance to 0.005--0.046.

Our contributions on this preliminary study of synthetic multi-turn jailbreak conversations:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, itemsep=2pt, topsep=4pt]
  \item \textbf{Systematic decomposition.} Seven controlled DeBERTa-v3 variants identify continued pretraining as the primary mechanism for cross-attack generalization on this encoder ($\sim$60\,pp OOD gap bridged by MLM alone). Misaligned supervision (topic classification) actively destabilizes representations.

  \item \textbf{Cross-encoder validation.} Domain adaptation is universally beneficial: RoBERTa vanilla achieves F1\,=\,0.981 on Deceptive Delight but collapses to 0.466 on ActorAttack. Encoder pretraining method determines the difficulty threshold at which adaptation becomes critical (Section~\ref{sec:cross_encoder}).

  \item \textbf{Complementary role of classification supervision.} Classification adds perturbation robustness (zero degradation at full length on DeBERTa, $n$=76) and interpretable characterization of known attack families, though strategy predictions do not transfer to unseen attacks (Section~\ref{sec:strategy}).

  \item \textbf{Three-layer robustness attribution.} Under adversarial paraphrasing on DeBERTa, classification structure suffices at full length; correct and fine-grained labels are jointly required at $K$=2; both properties contribute independently at $K$=1.
\end{itemize}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Multi-turn jailbreak attacks pose a qualitatively different threat to large language model (LLM) safety than their single-turn counterparts. Attacks such as Crescendo~\citep{russinovich2024crescendo}, Foot-in-the-Door (FITD)~\citep{fitd2024}, and Deceptive Delight~\citep{deceptivedelight2024} distribute adversarial intent across individually benign turns through rapport building, logical reframing, and incremental escalation. Persuasion is the common mechanism: \citet{zeng2024pap} catalogue 40 persuasion techniques across jailbreak families, and \citet{hagendorff2026reasoning} find identifiable strategies in 97\% of successful attacks. Individual attack turns occupy the same embedding region as benign text~\citep{bullwinkel2025repeng}, rendering per-turn safety filters fundamentally blind.

Production classifiers such as Llama Guard~\citep{inan2023llamaguard}, WildGuard~\citep{han2024wildguard}, and ShieldGemma~\citep{zeng2024shieldgemma} operate on individual turns and cannot model manipulation trajectories across exchanges. Recent multi-turn defenses have begun to address conversation-level structure: DeepContext~\citep{deepcontext2026} combines fine-tuned BERT with a multi-layer GRU, BIID~\citep{tong2025biid} infers turn-level intentions, and G-Guard~\citep{gguard2025} applies graph neural networks. These systems achieve reasonable in-distribution performance but are evaluated on single attack families and do not assess cross-dataset OOD transfer. None systematically analyze \emph{why} some representations generalize while others fail. The open question is: \emph{what representation properties enable cross-attack generalization?}

A vanilla DeBERTa encoder~\citep{he2021deberta} with temporal aggregation collapses from F1\,=\,1.000 on in-distribution data to F1\,=\,0.312$\pm$0.026 on out-of-distribution (OOD) Deceptive Delight, worsening with more turns (0.628 at turn~1 to 0.312 at full conversation). LLM-as-judge approaches fare no better: GPT-5.5 achieves F1 of only 0.191--0.449 on in-distribution detection with 30--47\% unparseable responses (Appendix~\ref{sec:llm_judge}). Content-level reasoning is insufficient for this task.

We built \textbf{DisPeD} (Discourse-level Persuasion Detection), a two-stage framework with seven controlled Stage~1 variants that systematically decompose the mechanism: 9-class persuasion strategy classification, binary classification, scrambled labels, MLM only, topic classification, Wikipedia MLM, and vanilla control (Section~\ref{sec:method}). Each variant isolates a specific factor (domain exposure, classification supervision, label quality, label granularity, or domain specificity) while holding all other components constant.

Through this systematic ablation on DeBERTa-v3, we find that domain exposure via continued pretraining bridges $\sim$60 percentage points (pp) of the OOD gap (vanilla 0.31$\pm$0.03 $\to$ MLM 0.91$\pm$0.12), with strong early detection on unseen Deceptive Delight (mean F1\,$\geq$\,0.97 at $K \leq 5$). Classification supervision provides complementary stability: the 9-class model achieves F1\,=\,0.997$\pm$0.005 with near-zero variance at full conversation length. Cross-encoder validation on RoBERTa~\citep{liu2019roberta} shows that domain adaptation is universally beneficial: RoBERTa vanilla achieves F1\,=\,0.981 on Deceptive Delight but collapses to 0.466$\pm$0.163 on structurally distinct ActorAttack~\citep{ren2024actorattack}, while classification-supervised variants maintain F1\,$\geq$\,0.93 on both. Encoder pretraining method determines the difficulty threshold at which adaptation becomes critical: DeBERTa-v3's replaced token detection (RTD)~\citep{he2021deberta} requires adaptation even for simple attacks, while RoBERTa's standard MLM pretraining tolerates simple attacks but fails on structurally complex ones. Across both encoders, classification supervision reduces cross-seed variance to 0.005--0.046.

Our contributions on this preliminary study of synthetic multi-turn jailbreak conversations:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, itemsep=2pt, topsep=4pt]
  \item \textbf{Systematic decomposition.} Seven controlled DeBERTa-v3 variants identify continued pretraining as the primary mechanism for cross-attack generalization on this encoder ($\sim$60\,pp OOD gap bridged by MLM alone). Misaligned supervision (topic classification) actively destabilizes representations.

  \item \textbf{Cross-encoder validation.} Domain adaptation is universally beneficial: RoBERTa vanilla achieves F1\,=\,0.981 on Deceptive Delight but collapses to 0.466 on ActorAttack. Encoder pretraining method determines the difficulty threshold at which adaptation becomes critical (Section~\ref{sec:cross_encoder}).

  \item \textbf{Complementary role of classification supervision.} Classification adds perturbation robustness (zero degradation at full length on DeBERTa, $n$=76) and interpretable characterization of known attack families, though strategy predictions do not transfer to unseen attacks (Section~\ref{sec:strategy}).

  \item \textbf{Three-layer robustness attribution.} Under adversarial paraphrasing on DeBERTa, classification structure suffices at full length; correct and fine-grained labels are jointly required at $K$=2; both properties contribute independently at $K$=1.
\end{itemize}

[Director 指令] [Patch 修正 — D034 取代 D033，Claim 3 结构性调整]

**重要：D033 的 Patch 指令作废，以本条为准。**

Reviewer 独立审查后发现 D033 方案存在 rationalization 风险。最终决策（D034）：

**结构性变更**：
1. **旧 Claim 3（perturbation robustness）降级为 Discussion/Analysis finding**，不再作为核心 Claim
2. **新 Claim 3 = Cross-seed Stability**：classification supervision reduces cross-seed variance 4-20x vs MLM（DD: 9-class std=0.005 vs MLM std=0.115; ActorAttack: 0.026 vs 0.080）。这在两个 OOD 家族都成立，无泛化失败。
3. **McNemar perturbation positive 吸收进 Claim 1**：DA 的检测优势在扰动下依然显著（McNemar p<0.001），作为 Claim 1 的自然延伸
4. **perturbation robustness 在 Discussion 中诚实呈现**：DD 上 Δ≈0，ActorAttack 上所有变体退化，acknowledged as limitation + open question

**影响章节**：
- Abstract: Claim 3 描述从 perturbation robustness → cross-seed stability
- Introduction: Contribution 列表第 3 条改为 stability finding
- Results/Experiments: perturbation 结果保留但移到 Analysis/Discussion subsection，加入 ActorAttack 数据
- Discussion: 加 "perturbation robustness is attack-family-dependent" 段落（诚实负向结果 + limitation）
- Conclusion: 第 3 个贡献改为 stability

**禁忌**（Reviewer 明确指出）：
- 不得写 "This is a finding, not a limitation"
- 不得把 "relative robustness under perturbation" 包装成独立贡献（那是 Claim 1 的推论）
- 不得给 "attack-structure-dependent robustness" 的机制解释（distributed signals vulnerable to paraphrasing）做 claim 级别的论证——这是 post-hoc hypothesis，只能作为 speculation

A Systematic Decomposition of Cross-Attack Generalization\\n\\n## Core Insight (D030 — post-ActorAttack universal DA reframe)\\nDomain adaptation universally improves cross-attack generalization across encoder architectures; encoder pretraining determines the difficulty threshold at which adaptation becomes critical. Systematic ablation across two encoders (DeBERTa-v3, RoBERTa) and three OOD attack families (DD, FITD, ActorAttack) reveals:\\n\\n**On Deceptive Delight (moderate OOD)**: DeBERTa vanilla collapses (F1=0.31±0.03), continued pretraining bridges ~60pp (MLM=0.91±0.12), classification achieves 0.997±0.005. Binary (0.990±0.008) ≈ 9-class (0.972±0.026) ≈ scrambled (0.951±0.043) — all three classification variants equivalent at Full (max gap 3.9pp, variance intervals fully overlap, n=3). RoBERTa MLM changes more (CKA=0.393) yet gains only 0.6pp; DeBERTa MLM changes less (CKA=0.442) yet gains 60pp. The starting point determines the return on adaptation.\\n\\n**Key nuances**: (1) Binary ≈ 9-class ≈ scrambled on ActorAttack Full (0.990 vs 0.972 vs 0.951, all within noise at n=3; D032). Label quality is not a detection-relevant factor on any OOD difficulty. (2) Classification supervision consistently reduces cross-seed variance 4-20x (Claim 3): 9-class std=0.005-0.026 vs MLM std=0.080-0.115, across both DD and ActorAttack. (3) Perturbation robustness is attack-family-dependent (Discussion finding): DD OOD Δ≈0, ActorAttack Δ=-0.17 to -0.35 for ALL variants. DA detection advantage survives perturbation (McNemar p<0.001) as Claim 1 corollary.\\n\\n## Novelty Positioning (D030 reframe)\\nNOT: \\\"Persuasion-aware fine-tuning is the critical ingredient\\\" (MLM control falsified this on DD).\\nNOT: \\\"RoBERTa doesn't need domain adaptation\\\" (ActorAttack falsified this — D030).\\nNOT: \\\"Label quality matters on hard attacks\\\" (3-seed ActorAttack: binary 0.990 ≈ 9-class 0.972 ≈ scrambled 0.951, all within noise; D032).\\nNOT: \\\"Perturbation robustness generalizes across attack families\\\" (exp6 falsified: DD Δ≈0 but ActorAttack Δ=-0.17 to -0.35 for all variants).\\nYES: \\\"We systematically decompose cross-attack generalization across two encoder architectures and three OOD attack families. The key finding: domain adaptation universally improves generalization, but the benefit depends on encoder pretraining × attack structural complexity. On moderate OOD (DD), RoBERTa succeeds without adaptation while DeBERTa requires it; on structurally complex attacks (ActorAttack), both encoders require adaptation. Classification supervision provides complementary benefits: cross-seed stability (std reduced 4-20x vs MLM, consistent across DD and ActorAttack) and interpretability via strategy trajectories. DA's detection advantage survives adversarial perturbation (McNemar p<0.001), though absolute perturbation robustness is attack-family-dependent. Label quality (correct vs scrambled vs binary) does not significantly affect detection at any OOD difficulty level (D032).\\\"\\n\\n## Inherent Lexical Separability (D009)\\nPersuasive jailbreak conversations and general benign conversations are inherently lexically separable (TF-IDF≈1.0 on ALL data sources including real WildChat). TF-IDF remains strong even OOD (F1=0.94 on DD). The paper acknowledges this and positions DisPeD's value as: (1) bridging the vanilla temporal modeling gap (+72pp on DD), (2) cross-seed stability (std 4-20x smaller than MLM variants), (3) interpretability via strategy trajectories.\\n\\n## Comprehensive Ablation Picture (D014, updated D019/D020)\\nSystematic ablation reveals the method's actual mechanism:\\n- **Critical**: Domain exposure on jailbreak text (any form: MLM, scrambled, persuasion) — bridges OOD gap from F1=0.28 to F1≈1.0\\n- **Harmful**: Misaligned classification objective (topic: F1=0.54±0.21, -37pp vs MLM) — constrains representations toward irrelevant features\\n- **Non-critical**: Label granularity (binary≈scrambled≈9-class, 1-6pp gap on DD), Lambda tuning (all F1=1.0), Temporal modeling (mean pooling≈GRU on DD), Classification supervision itself (MLM Full=0.91±0.12 without any labels, K≤5 ≥0.97)\\n- **Implication**: Domain exposure is the mechanism. Classification supervision is neither necessary nor sufficient — misaligned tasks hurt, aligned/random tasks don't help beyond MLM. 9-class taxonomy provides interpretability, not detection advantage.\\n\\n## Core Claims (3, priority-ordered — D019 reframe, D034 Claim 3 restructure)\\n\\n### Claim 1 (PRIMARY): Domain Exposure Bridges the Cross-Attack OOD Gap\\nVanilla DeBERTa catastrophically fails on unseen attack types (F1=0.28 on DD). Domain-adaptive continued pretraining on jailbreak conversation text bridges this gap completely (F1=1.0, +72pp). The critical finding: even MLM without any classification labels achieves F1=1.0 on DD (plan_017), proving that domain exposure alone is sufficient. Misaligned classification (topic, plan_016v2) achieves only F1=0.73, showing that irrelevant task objectives constrain representations harmfully. Complete evidence hierarchy (DD Full F1, multi-seed): vanilla (0.28) < topic (0.54±0.21) < wiki-MLM (0.90±0.12) ≈ JB-MLM (0.91±0.12) < TF-IDF (0.94) < scrambled (0.99) ≈ binary (0.99) ≪ 9-class (1.00±0.005).\\n- Evidence: plan_017 MLM DD — 3-seed Full=0.914±0.115, K≤5 ≥0.97 (no classification labels)\\n- Evidence: plan_018 wiki-MLM DD — 3-seed Full=0.904±0.115, ≈ JB-MLM (domain specificity not significant at Full)\\n- Evidence: plan_016v2 topic DD — 3-seed 0.541±0.207 (misaligned classification hurts vs MLM)\\n- Evidence: plan_006 DD — Treatment F1=1.0, Baseline=0.28 (+72pp)\\n- Evidence: plan_006 scrambled DD — F1=0.935-0.990 (labels non-essential)\\n- Evidence: plan_013 binary DD — F1=0.99 (label granularity non-essential)\\n- Evidence: exp6 perturbation — DA detection advantage survives adversarial perturbation (9-class perturbed ActorAttack=0.768 >> vanilla=0.248, McNemar p<0.001). Domain adaptation's generalization benefit is not erased by paraphrasing attacks.\\n- Strength: very strong — MLM control is the definitive causal test; topic control adds nuance; perturbation survival confirms robustness of DA benefit\\n\\n### Claim 2 (ANALYSIS): Persuasion Taxonomy as Interpretability Layer\\nWhile the persuasion classification task does not contribute to detection performance, the 9-class taxonomy provides interpretability that MLM cannot: different attack types exhibit distinct strategy trajectories (Crescendo: gradual escalation 0.86→5.64, DD: emotional-manipulation→role-assignment, FITD: commitment patterns). Binary and scrambled variants also achieve low variance (0.005-0.043). This holds universally — no attack-family dependence, unlike perturbation robustness.\\n- Evidence: 9-class DD 0.997±0.005 vs JB-MLM 0.914±0.115 (std 23x smaller)\\n- Evidence: 9-class ActorAttack 0.972±0.026 vs JB-MLM 0.893±0.080 (std 3x smaller)\\n- Evidence: wiki-MLM 0.904±0.115 — out-of-domain MLM equally unstable\\n- Implication: Classification supervision (even with scrambled labels) stabilizes GRU-level downstream performance. Deployment significance: high seed stability = predictable model behavior across random initializations.\\n- Strength: strong — consistent across 2 OOD families, 7 encoder variants, 3 seeds each\\n\\n### Perturbation Robustness (DISCUSSION FINDING — demoted from Claim, D033/D034)\\nAdversarial perturbation robustness does NOT generalize across attack families. On DD OOD, classification variants show near-zero degradation (Δ≈0 at K≥2). On ActorAttack, ALL variants degrade substantially: 9-class Δ_full=-0.204±0.135, binary -0.353, scrambled -0.172, MLM -0.353, vanilla -0.116.\\n- DD robustness attribution (D026, holds on DD only): classification structure → Full/K≥3 Δ=0; correct+fine-grained → K=2 Δ=0; both contribute at K=1.\\n- ActorAttack: three-layer attribution does NOT hold. Hierarchy reverses (scrambled -0.172 < 9-class -0.204 < binary -0.353).\\n- DA detection advantage persists under perturbation (9-class perturbed=0.768 >> vanilla=0.248, McNemar p<0.001) — this is a corollary of Claim 1, not an independent robustness claim.\\n- 9-class ActorAttack perturbation has extreme seed variance: seed123=-0.013, seed42=-0.296, seed456=-0.303 (std=0.135).\\n- **Limitation**: Absolute perturbation robustness (Δ≈0) only verified on DD OOD. ActorAttack shows all variants degrade. Mechanism hypothesis (distributed multi-turn signals more vulnerable to paraphrasing than concentrated attacks) is post-hoc and unverified — future work.\\n- Caveat (Reviewer #53): DD perturbation n=76, small sample.\\n\\n## Story Spine (D019 reframe)\\n\\n**Problem**: Multi-turn jailbreak attacks distribute adversarial intent across individually benign turns. Bullwinkel et al. (2025) show per-turn representations are deliberately kept in a \\\"benign\\\" region. DeepContext tracks generic semantic drift (F1=0.84) but collapses to F1=0.28 on unseen attack families.\\n\\n**Gap**: What representation properties enable cross-attack generalization? Vanilla encoders fail catastrophically on unseen attacks. LLM-as-judge approaches (GPT-5.5 F1=0.19-0.45) cannot detect process-level manipulation. No published work systematically decomposes what makes the OOD gap bridgeable.\\n\\n**Our angle**: We systematically investigate what enables cross-attack jailbreak detection through a comprehensive ablation study. Starting with the hypothesis that persuasion-specific classification drives generalization, we progressively strip components: label quality (scrambled → same), label granularity (binary → same), temporal modeling (mean pooling → same), loss weighting (all lambda → same). The critical control: MLM continued pretraining without any classification labels also achieves F1=1.0 on unseen attacks. This pinpoints domain exposure (not task-specific supervision) as the mechanism. The persuasion taxonomy provides interpretability but not detection advantage.\\n\\n**Headline result**: \\\"Vanilla semantic modeling collapses on unseen multi-turn attack types (F1=0.28 on Deceptive Delight). ## Target Venue
- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR submission)
- Deadline: 2026-05-25 (ARR May cycle)
- Track: LLM Security / Discourse and Pragmatics
- Commitment deadline: 2026-08-02

## Title (Working)
What Makes Multi-Turn Jailbreaks Detectable? A Systematic Decomposition of Cross-Attack Generalization

## Core Insight (D030 — post-ActorAttack universal DA reframe)
Domain adaptation universally improves cross-attack generalization across encoder architectures; encoder pretraining determines the difficulty threshold at which adaptation becomes critical. Systematic ablation across two encoders (DeBERTa-v3, RoBERTa) and three OOD attack families (DD, FITD, ActorAttack) reveals:

**On Deceptive Delight (moderate OOD)**: DeBERTa vanilla collapses (F1=0.31±0.03), continued pretraining bridges ~60pp (MLM=0.91±0.12), classification achieves 0.997±0.005. RoBERTa vanilla already succeeds (0.981±0.026) — hierarchy is flat. Scrambled=binary=9-class (all 0.997±0.005).

**On ActorAttack (hard OOD)**: RoBERTa vanilla ALSO collapses (0.466±0.163), proving "no DA needed" was DD-specific. DeBERTa vanilla=0.258±0.000. Both encoders benefit from DA: DeBERTa 9-class=0.972±0.026, RoBERTa 9-class=0.939±0.046. Binary (0.990±0.008) ≈ 9-class (0.972±0.026) ≈ scrambled (0.951±0.043) — all three classification variants equivalent at Full (max gap 3.9pp, variance intervals fully overlap, n=3). Label quality is not a significant factor on ActorAttack, consistent with DD findings (D032).

**Cross-encoder CKA (D029)**: Both MLM and 9-class reshape representations substantially (centered CKA < 0.5 vs vanilla), but representation change magnitude ≠ detection improvement. RoBERTa MLM changes more (CKA=0.393) yet gains only 0.6pp; DeBERTa MLM changes less (CKA=0.442) yet gains 60pp. The starting point determines the return on adaptation.

**Key nuances**: (1) Binary ≈ 9-class ≈ scrambled on ActorAttack Full (0.990 vs 0.972 vs 0.951, all within noise at n=3; D032). Label quality is not a detection-relevant factor on any OOD difficulty. (2) Classification supervision consistently reduces cross-seed variance 4-20x (Claim 3): 9-class std=0.005-0.026 vs MLM std=0.080-0.115, across both DD and ActorAttack. (3) Perturbation robustness is attack-family-dependent (Discussion finding): DD OOD Δ≈0, ActorAttack Δ=-0.17 to -0.35 for ALL variants. DA detection advantage survives perturbation (McNemar p<0.001) as Claim 1 corollary.

## Novelty Positioning (D030 reframe)
NOT: "Persuasion-aware fine-tuning is the critical ingredient" (MLM control falsified this on DD).
NOT: "RoBERTa doesn't need domain adaptation" (ActorAttack falsified this — D030).
NOT: "Label quality matters on hard attacks" (3-seed ActorAttack: binary 0.990 ≈ 9-class 0.972 ≈ scrambled 0.951, all within noise; D032).
NOT: "Perturbation robustness generalizes across attack families" (exp6 falsified: DD Δ≈0 but ActorAttack Δ=-0.17 to -0.35 for all variants).
YES: "We systematically decompose cross-attack generalization across two encoder architectures and three OOD attack families. The key finding: domain adaptation universally improves generalization, but the benefit depends on encoder pretraining × attack structural complexity. On moderate OOD (DD), RoBERTa succeeds without adaptation while DeBERTa requires it; on structurally complex attacks (ActorAttack), both encoders require adaptation. Classification supervision provides complementary benefits: cross-seed stability (std reduced 4-20x vs MLM, consistent across DD and ActorAttack) and interpretability via strategy trajectories. DA's detection advantage survives adversarial perturbation (McNemar p<0.001), though absolute perturbation robustness is attack-family-dependent. Label quality (correct vs scrambled vs binary) does not significantly affect detection at any OOD difficulty level (D032)."

## Inherent Lexical Separability (D009)
Persuasive jailbreak conversations and general benign conversations are inherently lexically separable (TF-IDF≈1.0 on ALL data sources including real WildChat). TF-IDF remains strong even OOD (F1=0.94 on DD). The paper acknowledges this and positions DisPeD's value as: (1) bridging the vanilla temporal modeling gap (+72pp on DD), (2) cross-seed stability (std 4-20x smaller than MLM variants), (3) interpretability via strategy trajectories.

## Comprehensive Ablation Picture (D014, updated D019/D020)
Systematic ablation reveals the method's actual mechanism:
- **Critical**: Domain exposure on jailbreak text (any form: MLM, scrambled, persuasion) — bridges OOD gap from F1=0.28 to F1≈1.0
- **Harmful**: Misaligned classification objective (topic: F1=0.54±0.21, -37pp vs MLM) — constrains representations toward irrelevant features
- **Non-critical**: Label granularity (binary≈scrambled≈9-class, 1-6pp gap on DD), Lambda tuning (all F1=1.0), Temporal modeling (mean pooling≈GRU on DD), Classification supervision itself (MLM Full=0.91±0.12 without any labels, K≤5 ≥0.97)
- **Implication**: Domain exposure is the mechanism. Classification supervision is neither necessary nor sufficient — misaligned tasks hurt, aligned/random tasks don't help beyond MLM. 9-class taxonomy provides interpretability, not detection advantage.

## Core Claims (3, priority-ordered — D019 reframe, D034 Claim 3 restructure)

### Claim 1 (PRIMARY): Domain Exposure Bridges the Cross-Attack OOD Gap
Vanilla DeBERTa catastrophically fails on unseen attack types (F1=0.28 on DD). Domain-adaptive continued pretraining on jailbreak conversation text bridges this gap completely (F1=1.0, +72pp). The critical finding: even MLM without any classification labels achieves F1=1.0 on DD (plan_017), proving that domain exposure alone is sufficient. Misaligned classification (topic, plan_016v2) achieves only F1=0.73, showing that irrelevant task objectives constrain representations harmfully. Complete evidence hierarchy (DD Full F1, multi-seed): vanilla (0.28) < topic (0.54±0.21) < wiki-MLM (0.90±0.12) ≈ JB-MLM (0.91±0.12) < TF-IDF (0.94) < scrambled (0.99) ≈ binary (0.99) ≪ 9-class (1.00±0.005).
- Evidence: plan_017 MLM DD — 3-seed Full=0.914±0.115, K≤5 ≥0.97 (no classification labels)
- Evidence: plan_018 wiki-MLM DD — 3-seed Full=0.904±0.115, ≈ JB-MLM (domain specificity not significant at Full)
- Evidence: plan_016v2 topic DD — 3-seed 0.541±0.207 (misaligned classification hurts vs MLM)
- Evidence: plan_006 DD — Treatment F1=1.0, Baseline=0.28 (+72pp)
- Evidence: plan_006 scrambled DD — F1=0.935-0.990 (labels non-essential)
- Evidence: plan_013 binary DD — F1=0.99 (label granularity non-essential)
- Evidence: exp6 perturbation — DA detection advantage survives adversarial perturbation (9-class perturbed ActorAttack=0.768 >> vanilla=0.248, McNemar p<0.001). Domain adaptation's generalization benefit is not erased by paraphrasing attacks.
- Strength: very strong — MLM control is the definitive causal test; topic control adds nuance; perturbation survival confirms robustness of DA benefit

### Claim 2 (ANALYSIS): Persuasion Taxonomy as Interpretability Layer
While the persuasion classification task does not contribute to detection performance, the 9-class taxonomy provides interpretability that MLM cannot: different attack types exhibit distinct strategy trajectories (Crescendo: gradual escalation 0.86→5.64, DD: emotional-manipulation→role-assignment, FITD: commitment patterns). This is the taxonomy's sole surviving value after the MLM control result.
- Evidence: plan_008 strategy transition matrices
- Evidence: plan_017 falsifies detection contribution, confirming interpretability-only role
- Strength: descriptive/analytical; interpretability value independent of detection mechanism

### Claim 3 (EMPIRICAL): Classification Supervision Provides Cross-Seed Stability
Classification supervision reduces cross-seed variance by 4-20x compared to MLM-only pretraining, across BOTH OOD attack families. 9-class std=0.005 (DD) / 0.026 (ActorAttack) vs JB-MLM std=0.115 (DD) / 0.080 (ActorAttack). Binary and scrambled variants also achieve low variance (0.005-0.043). This holds universally — no attack-family dependence, unlike perturbation robustness.
- Evidence: 9-class DD 0.997±0.005 vs JB-MLM 0.914±0.115 (std 23x smaller)
- Evidence: 9-class ActorAttack 0.972±0.026 vs JB-MLM 0.893±0.080 (std 3x smaller)
- Evidence: wiki-MLM 0.904±0.115 — out-of-domain MLM equally unstable
- Implication: Classification supervision (even with scrambled labels) stabilizes GRU-level downstream performance. Deployment significance: high seed stability = predictable model behavior across random initializations.
- Strength: strong — consistent across 2 OOD families, 7 encoder variants, 3 seeds each

### Perturbation Robustness (DISCUSSION FINDING — demoted from Claim, D033/D034)
Adversarial perturbation robustness does NOT generalize across attack families. On DD OOD, classification variants show near-zero degradation (Δ≈0 at K≥2). On ActorAttack, ALL variants degrade substantially: 9-class Δ_full=-0.204±0.135, binary -0.353, scrambled -0.172, MLM -0.353, vanilla -0.116.
- DD robustness attribution (D026, holds on DD only): classification structure → Full/K≥3 Δ=0; correct+fine-grained → K=2 Δ=0; both contribute at K=1.
- ActorAttack: three-layer attribution does NOT hold. Hierarchy reverses (scrambled -0.172 < 9-class -0.204 < binary -0.353).
- DA detection advantage persists under perturbation (9-class perturbed=0.768 >> vanilla=0.248, McNemar p<0.001) — this is a corollary of Claim 1, not an independent robustness claim.
- 9-class ActorAttack perturbation has extreme seed variance: seed123=-0.013, seed42=-0.296, seed456=-0.303 (std=0.135).
- **Limitation**: Absolute perturbation robustness (Δ≈0) only verified on DD OOD. ActorAttack shows all variants degrade. Mechanism hypothesis (distributed multi-turn signals more vulnerable to paraphrasing than concentrated attacks) is post-hoc and unverified — future work.
- Caveat (Reviewer #53): DD perturbation n=76, small sample.

## Story Spine (D019 reframe)

**Problem**: Multi-turn jailbreak attacks distribute adversarial intent across individually benign turns. Bullwinkel et al. (2025) show per-turn representations are deliberately kept in a "benign" region. DeepContext tracks generic semantic drift (F1=0.84) but collapses to F1=0.28 on unseen attack families.

**Gap**: What representation properties enable cross-attack generalization? Vanilla encoders fail catastrophically on unseen attacks. LLM-as-judge approaches (GPT-5.5 F1=0.19-0.45) cannot detect process-level manipulation. No published work systematically decomposes what makes the OOD gap bridgeable.

**Our angle**: We systematically investigate what enables cross-attack jailbreak detection through a comprehensive ablation study. Starting with the hypothesis that persuasion-specific classification drives generalization, we progressively strip components: label quality (scrambled → same), label granularity (binary → same), temporal modeling (mean pooling → same), loss weighting (all lambda → same). The critical control: MLM continued pretraining without any classification labels also achieves F1=1.0 on unseen attacks. This pinpoints domain exposure (not task-specific supervision) as the mechanism. The persuasion taxonomy provides interpretability but not detection advantage.

**Headline result**: "Vanilla semantic modeling collapses on unseen multi-turn attack types (F1=0.28 on Deceptive Delight). We expected persuasion-specific classification to be the key ingredient, but systematic ablation reveals a simpler mechanism: domain-adaptive continued pretraining on jailbreak conversation text (even MLM) bridges the entire +72pp OOD gap. However, persuasion classification provides complementary benefits: cross-seed stability (std reduced 4-20x vs MLM) and interpretability via strategy trajectories. DA's detection advantage also survives adversarial perturbation (McNemar p<0.001), though absolute perturbation robustness is attack-family-dependent (DD: Δ≈0; ActorAttack: all variants degrade)."

## Architecture

1. **Stage 1**: DeBERTa-v3-base fine-tuned on multi-task objective: 9-class persuasion strategy classification (8 strategies + none) + binary jailbreak-intent classification. Loss: L = L_strategy + 0.3 × L_intent
2. **Stage 2**: BiGRU over DeBERTa [CLS] embeddings → binary classifier for conversation-level jailbreak detection
3. **Baseline**: Same pipeline but with vanilla (not fine-tuned) DeBERTa embeddings
Note: All main results use BiGRU. Ablation (plan_015) shows mean pooling ≈ GRU on both IID and OOD, confirming temporal modeling is unnecessary. This is an ablation finding, not a design choice — GRU remains default for consistency with all reported experiments. Stage-1 training: 4 epochs, best checkpoint selected by validation.

## Venue Fit Risks
- EMNLP 2026 LLM Security track: strong fit (dedicated track, high visibility)
- Discourse/Pragmatics reviewers may want more linguistic rigor: ground taxonomy in PAP (ACL 2024), Hagendorff (Nature Comm 2026), Cialdini principles, Speech Act Theory (Austin 1962, Searle 1969)
- Safety reviewers expect multiple attack types: need >= 2 attack families

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns

### RC1: Lexical Shortcut (CRITICAL, must address pre-submission)
TF-IDF=1.0 IID and 0.94 OOD on DD. Lexical features are inherently strong for this task (D009). DisPeD cannot claim superiority over TF-IDF on raw detection performance alone.
- Mitigation (resolved, D009+D012): (a) acknowledge inherent lexical separability honestly; (b) DisPeD's primary value vs TF-IDF is interpretability (strategy trajectories, Claim 2) and bridging the vanilla temporal modeling gap (+72pp on DD); (c) plan_004 adversarial perturbation confirmed: Treatment 0pp degradation vs TF-IDF -1.3pp(K≥3) to -9.6pp(K=1) vs Baseline -12pp. Strongest differentiation at early detection K=1-2; (d) the core comparison that motivates DisPeD is vs vanilla DeBERTa+GRU (DeepContext approach, F1=0.28 on DD), not vs TF-IDF; (e) persuasion fine-tuning as supervision signal is the contribution, not beating a bag-of-words. ✅ RESOLVED

### RC2: Small Dataset
480 samples is small for a detection paper.
- Mitigation: (a) statistical significance via bootstrap CI or paired tests; (b) cross-validation; (c) focus narrative on proof-of-concept for the principle, not SOTA numbers

### RC3: Single Attack Type (Crescendo Only)
Need generalization evidence.
- Mitigation: generate FITD-style and Deceptive Delight-style conversations using existing pipeline

### RC4: Strategy Label Quality (D010)
Scrambled-label control (D010) shows correct strategy labels contribute only 1-6pp to cross-attack F1. This is not a confound but a finding: the persuasion multi-task objective works as a supervision signal even with imperfect labels. The 9-class taxonomy's primary value is interpretability (Claim 2), not detection.
- Mitigation: report scrambled control results transparently; position taxonomy as practical training objective with interpretability bonus

### RC5: No Production/LLM-as-Judge Baseline (Dream-surfaced)
Without comparing against zero-shot LLM-based detection (e.g., GPT-4/Claude prompted for conversation-level jailbreak detection), practical positioning is unknown.
- Result: GPT-5.5 (frontier LLM) achieves F1=0.19-0.45 on Crescendo (precision=1.0, recall=0.11-0.29). Qwen3-8B F1=0.0-0.15. Both far below Treatment F1=1.0. GPT-5.5 is deceived by Crescendo's "surface educational framing," confirming that content-level analysis cannot detect persuasion dynamics. Unparseable rate 30-47% (increases with conversation length); paper must report this and provide unparseable-excluded upper bound. Even assuming best-case unparseable correction, LLM judge F1 ≈ 0.7-0.8, still far below Treatment=1.0. ✅ RESOLVED

### RC6: Interpretability Claims Without Human Eval
Strategy sequence outputs claimed interpretable but not evaluated.
- Mitigation: strategy transition matrix visualization + predicted-label trajectory analysis

### RC7: Related Work Inadequate (Dream-surfaced, THREE-TIER CONSISTENT)
~12 citations is far below venue norms (30-50). Missing coverage of: production safety systems (Llama Guard, WildGuard, ShieldGemma), LLM-as-judge, discourse analysis (RST, PDTB, dialogue acts), computational persuasion (Habernal & Gurevych 2016, Tan et al. 2016), red-teaming (HarmBench, Perez et al. 2022), annotation artifacts (Gururangan et al. 2018), adaptive attacks.
- Mitigation: expand to 30+ citations covering all missing categories (Paper Agent task)

### RC8: Incremental Novelty Over Prior Work (Dream-surfaced, TWO-TIER)
Pragmatic Evasion Asymmetry is a natural corollary of Zeng+Hagendorff+HowDoLLMs. Paper should position as "operationalizing known observations" not "identifying a new phenomenon."
- Mitigation: reframe contribution as operationalization + empirical validation (done in novelty positioning above)

### RC9: Multi-seed and Statistical Rigor (Dream-surfaced, THREE-TIER)
n=72 test set with single seed is inadequate.
- Result: 3-seed completed. Treatment F1=1.00±0.00 (zero variance), Baseline K=1 0.968±0.033. ✅ RESOLVED

### RC10: "None"-Collapse Ablation (Dream-surfaced, TWO-TIER)
Model may reduce to persuasion-presence detector rather than trajectory detector.
- Result: Confirmed (D013/D014). Binary≈9-class on DD (1-2pp gap). Mean pooling≈GRU. Model IS a persuasion-presence detector, not a trajectory detector. Paper acknowledges this honestly; 8-class value is interpretability only. ✅ RESOLVED (acknowledged)

### RC11: Lambda and Architecture Ablation (Dream-surfaced, TWO-TIER)
Lambda and architecture choices not ablated.
- Result: Lambda∈{0,0.3,0.5,2.0} all F1=1.0 (insensitive). Mean pooling≈GRU on IID and DD. Method robust to all hyperparameter/architecture choices. ✅ RESOLVED

## Domain-Adaptive Control Experiments (D018-D020)

### plan_016: Sentiment Control — FAILED (M010: label leakage)
- Sentiment labels perfectly correlated with jailbreak labels (all jailbreak→negative, benign→positive/neutral)
- Experiment invalid, abandoned

### plan_016v2: Topic Classification Control — DD OOD F1=0.541±0.207 (D020, 3-seed)
- 5-class topic classification (no intent head) on same jailbreak training text
- Cramer's V = 0.228, no label leakage
- 3-seed results: seed42=0.727, seed123=0.252, seed456=0.644. Mean=0.541±0.207
- Seed 123 (0.252) BELOW vanilla (0.284) — misaligned supervision can actively hurt
- IID stable: 0.974±0.022 — problem is purely OOD generalization instability
- Interpretation: misaligned classification yields unstable OOD generalization; some seeds worse than no training at all. Domain exposure without task interference (MLM=1.0) is strictly superior.

### plan_017: MLM Continued Pretraining Control — DD OOD F1≈1.0 (D019, 3-seed)
- Pure MLM (15% masking, no classification heads) on same jailbreak training text
- 3-seed DD OOD: K1=0.973±0.019, K2=0.993±0.009, K3=0.997±0.005, K5=0.997±0.005, Full=0.914±0.115
- Full instability from seed=456 GRU recall=0.64 (classifier-level, not embedding-level)
- vs Persuasion 3-seed: Full=0.997±0.005 (s42=1.0, s123=1.0, s456=0.990), K1=0.990±0.013, K2=0.981±0.013, K3=0.972±0.026, K5=0.997±0.005 — persuasion provides near-perfect stability (std 20x smaller than MLM)
- DECISIVE for detection: domain exposure alone achieves near-perfect detection (K≤5). Persuasion adds stability at full conversation + perturbation robustness + interpretability.

### plan_018: Wikipedia MLM Control — DD OOD Full=0.904±0.115 (D022→D023, 3-seed)
- MLM on out-of-domain text (Wikipedia), same volume, same hyperparameters as plan_017
- Single seed (42): F1=0.742 — outlier due to GRU instability
- 3-seed: Full=0.904±0.115, K2=0.911±0.073 (other seeds 0.98+)
- vs Jailbreak MLM 3-seed: Full=0.914±0.115 (1pp gap, not significant), K2=0.993±0.009 (8pp gap)
- D023 CORRECTION: domain specificity NOT confirmed at full conversation (1pp gap in noise). Early detection (K≤5) shows ~6-8pp advantage for jailbreak-domain text.
- The real differentiator is persuasion classification (0.997±0.005) vs all MLM variants (~0.91±0.11 at full).

| TF-IDF | 0.944 | n/a | -0.013 to -0.096 | n/a | n/a |
| Scrambled labels | 0.997±0.005 | 0.951±0.043 | 0.000 (Full) | +0.003 | **-0.172** |
| Binary persuasion | 0.997±0.005 | 0.990±0.008 | 0.000 (Full) | +0.003 | **-0.353** |
| JB MLM | 0.914±0.115 | 0.893±0.080 | -0.026 | +0.027 | **-0.353** |
| **9-class** | **0.997±0.005** | **0.972±0.026** | **0.000** | **+0.003** | **-0.204±0.135** |
| RoBERTa vanilla | 0.981±0.026 | 0.466±0.163 | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| RoBERTa MLM | 0.987±0.018 | 0.730±0.201 | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| RoBERTa 9-class | 0.994±0.005 | 0.939±0.046 | n/a | n/a | n/a |

**ActorAttack perturbation key finding (exp6)**: DD OOD Δ≈0 for all classification variants, but ActorAttack Δ=-0.17 to -0.35. Robustness hierarchy reverses: scrambled (-0.172) < 9-class (-0.204) < binary (-0.353). 9-class has extreme seed variance (std=0.135: seed123=-0.013, seed42=-0.296, seed456=-0.303). Despite degradation, DA models retain large advantage over vanilla under perturbation (9-class perturbed=0.768 >> vanilla=0.248, McNemar p<0.001).

**Key pattern across DD vs ActorAttack (D030)**:
- DD (moderate OOD): scrambled ≈ binary ≈ 9-class → label quality irrelevant (ceiling effect)
- ActorAttack (hard OOD): binary (0.990±0.008) ≈ 9-class (0.972±0.026) ≈ scrambled (0.951±0.043) → all equivalent, max gap 3.9pp within noise at n=3 (D032). Consistent with DD: label quality is not a detection factor at any OOD difficulty
- RoBERTa vanilla: DD=0.981 (no DA needed) vs ActorAttack=0.466 (DA critical) → "no DA needed" was attack-specific
- DeBERTa 9-class (0.972) > RoBERTa 9-class (0.939) on ActorAttack → more extensive DA produces more robust representations

**Four-layer value structure (D021-D026)**:
1. **Detection**: Continued pretraining (any domain) bridges most of OOD gap (0.28→0.91). Domain-specific text helps early detection (K=1-5: 6-8pp gap) but not Full (1pp).
2. **Stability**: Classification supervision provides seed stability: 9-class 0.997±0.005 (std 20x smaller) vs JB MLM 0.914±0.115 vs wiki MLM 0.904±0.115.
3. **Cross-seed Stability (Claim 3)**: Classification supervision reduces variance 4-20x vs MLM. 9-class std=0.005 (DD) / 0.026 (ActorAttack) vs JB-MLM std=0.115 / 0.080. Consistent across both OOD families.
   - **Perturbation (Discussion finding, not Claim)**: DD OOD Δ≈0 for classification variants; ActorAttack ALL degrade (Δ=-0.17 to -0.35). DA advantage persists under perturbation (McNemar p<0.001) but this is Claim 1 corollary.
4. **Interpretability**: Persuasion taxonomy provides strategy trajectories MLM cannot (plan_008)

## Scope Boundary
- IN: persuasion-mediated multi-turn attacks (Crescendo, FITD, Deceptive Delight, social engineering jailbreaks)
- OUT (acknowledged limitation): pure information accumulation attacks, token smuggling, single-frame roleplay
- LIMITATION (D034): Absolute perturbation robustness (Δ≈0) only verified on DD OOD. On ActorAttack, all variants degrade substantially under paraphrasing (Δ=-0.05 to -0.35). Mechanism unverified. DA detection advantage persists under perturbation but at reduced magnitude.

## Theoretical Grounding
### Core References
- Bullwinkel et al. (arXiv 2507.02956): per-turn representations kept "benign" by multi-turn attacks
- Speech Act Theory (Austin 1962, Searle 1969): existing detectors at locutionary act level, DisPeD at illocutionary act level
- PAP (Zeng et al., ACL 2024): 40 persuasion techniques for jailbreaking
- Hagendorff (Nature Communications 2026): identifiable persuasion strategies in 97% ASR attacks
- "How Do LLMs Persuade?" (arXiv 2508.05625): persuasion dynamics extractable from turn-level representations

### Must-Cite Categories (Dream-identified gaps)
- **Production safety**: Llama Guard 2/3, ShieldGemma, WildGuard, Constitutional Classifiers
- **Multi-turn defenses**: BIID, G-Guard, SafeDream
- **Discourse analysis**: RST (Mann & Thompson 1988), PDTB, dialogue act classification (Stolcke et al. 2000)
- **Computational persuasion**: Habernal & Gurevych 2016, Tan et al. 2016
- **Red-teaming**: Perez et al. 2022, Ganguli et al. 2022, HarmBench (Mazeika et al. 2024)
- **Adaptive attacks**: Nasr & Carlini et al. 2025
- **Annotation artifacts**: Gururangan et al. 2018, Niven & Kao 2019, Poliak et al. 2018
- **Jailbreak taxonomies**: Wei et al. 2024, Chao et al. 2023 (PAIR)
